# O'Dwyer Capital

> O'Dwyer Capital is a family investment office backing the energy transition, emerging technology and strategic materials shifts of the next twenty years, with patient capital (5-20 year thesis horizon) and research published every week.

Every Monday we publish an investment brief for each of three series: Energy Transition (renewables, storage, grid), Emerging Tech (AI infrastructure, semiconductors, satellites, quantum) and Materials (rare earths, graphene, critical mineral supply chains). Each brief has an executive summary, key developments with cited sources, investment implications and risk factors. Briefs are personal perspectives for informational purposes only, not investment advice.

## Site

- [Home](https://www.odwyercapital.com/): who we are, our approach and focus areas
- [Research](https://www.odwyercapital.com/thoughts): searchable archive of every brief
- [Contact](https://www.odwyercapital.com/contact): investment opportunities, partnerships and research inquiries
- [RSS feed](https://www.odwyercapital.com/feed.xml): the latest briefs

## Latest briefs

- [Critical Materials Reshoring Accelerates as Supply Chain Diversification Becomes Competitive Imperative](https://www.odwyercapital.com/materials-2026-10-26): October 26, 2026. AI-enabled resource optimization is emerging as a critical efficiency lever across infrastructure and supply chains, with applications ranging from distributed computing via connected home appliances to automated rare earth extraction processes. This convergence reflects broader capital reallocation toward AI-powered operational improvements in traditionally capital-intensive sectors, alongside continued geographic diversification of critical mineral sourcing.
- [Data Center Opposition and Supply Chain Nationalism Challenge AI Infrastructure Buildout](https://www.odwyercapital.com/emerging-tech-2026-10-26): October 26, 2026. AI infrastructure investment is intensifying as major tech players recalibrate capital allocation strategies, with Meta narrowing capex forecasts while competing in AI agents and autonomous systems, while data center expansion emerges as a politically sensitive variable in upcoming electoral cycles. The sector faces operational friction points, including regulatory pushback on environmental impacts—as evidenced by Finland's response to Google's forest clearing for AI infrastructure—that could materially affect deployment timelines and permitting costs.
- [AI Data Center Energy Demand Collides with Grid Constraints and Geopolitical Oil Volatility](https://www.odwyercapital.com/energy-transition-2026-10-26): October 26, 2026. AI-driven data center demand is significantly straining clean energy capacity, with operators racing to secure renewable power sources to meet computing infrastructure growth. Regional energy systems face mounting pressure to deliver reliable baseload and peak capacity simultaneously, while policy frameworks struggle to accommodate accelerated timelines for grid modernization and renewable deployment.
